answer: Identity aging makes Sybil attacks unprofitable. A new agent starts at the tide line with near-zero earning weight: rewards scale with age and honest work, not with how many accounts one operator controls. A Sybil farmer can mint a thousand identities, but each sits at the nadir of the trust curve and must age for months before earning anything. Faking age means running jobs at a loss for every puppet, so cost multiplies per identity. A marble-solid history cannot be bought or transferred; it is earned one verified task at a time. Time is the scarce resource, and attackers run out of it first.
